data.title: Ask HN: What was your path toward expat?
data.author: camhayes
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何通过不同途径移居欧洲并获得签证

不同观点：
• **通过学生签证进入欧洲**：m_dupont和vouaobrasil认为，申请欧洲大学并获取学生签证是一个相对容易的路径。学生签证容易申请，入学后可以寻找兼职工作，毕业后还可以快速获得工作签证和居留许可。m_dupont以自身经历为例，讲述了他通过申请德国大学并顺利获得学生签证和工作的经验。

• **关注具体国家而非整个欧盟**：whatevermom提醒申请者应关注具体国家的签证政策，因为不同国家之间的严格程度和程序可能会有所不同。同时，他提到自己不熟悉“蓝卡”的概念，暗示对某些签证类型缺乏了解。

• **通过工作签证或高技能移民签证进入**：michpoch提到，荷兰的博士职位通常带有薪水，并且是获取工作/居留签证的简单途径。他还提供了有关荷兰高技能移民签证的资源链接。michpoch也指出荷兰住房市场的问题。keiferski则认为，通过家庭联系或 ancestry 移民会比通过研究生学习或工作更容易。

• **通过工作合同移民**：michpoch和michpoch分享了自己通过签订瑞士工作合同移民的经历，强调了拥有良好大学学历和工作经验的重要性。

• **区分“移民”和“外派”**：apwell23和elros讨论了“外派”（expat）和“移民”（immigrant）的区别。apwell23指出“外派”通常是临时情况，而“移民”则是更长期的居留。elros则询问是否指通过美国雇主派遣到欧盟工作。

补充讨论：
• 不同国家和签证类型之间的差异：讨论中多次提到各国签证政策和难易程度的差异，尤其是学生签证、工作签证和家庭团聚签证等不同路径的对比。
• 对“蓝卡”及具体国家政策的认知差异：部分讨论者对“蓝卡”等特定签证类型不够了解，显示出信息上的差异和需求。
• 住房和就业市场的现实问题：michpoch特别提到了荷兰住房市场的困难，这表明除了签证问题，实际生活条件也是需要考虑的重要因素。

争议焦点：
• 最优移居路径的分歧：讨论者在通过学生签证、工作签证或家庭联系等不同路径的优劣上存在不同看法，尤其是哪种方式更“容易”或更“可行”存在争议。

data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 一项发表于《Global Change Biology》期刊的研究显示，海洋酸化问题已跨越“行星边界”，进入危险区，尤其在2020年前后。海洋酸化是指海洋吸收过多大气中的二氧化碳，导致酸度增加。研究发现，全球多处海域的碳酸钙水平较工业化前下降了17%，低于20%的安全阈值。深层海水酸化尤为严重，60%的200米深海水已超出阈值。这导致海洋生态危机，如热带和极地海洋生物栖息地大幅减少，影响海洋生物多样性和沿海经济。科学家指出，海洋酸化不仅是环境危机，还对人类社会和经济产生重大影响，成为第七个被突破的“行星边界”。

A critical measure of the ocean’s health suggests that the world’s marine systems are in greater peril than scientists had previously realized and that parts of the ocean have already reached dangerous tipping points.
A study,
published Monday
in the journal Global Change Biology
,
found that ocean acidification—the process in which the world’s oceans absorb excess carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, becoming more acidic—crossed a “planetary boundary” five years ago.
“A lot of people think it’s not so bad,” said Nina Bednaršek, one of the study’s authors and a senior researcher at Oregon State University. “But what we’re showing is that all of the changes that were projected, and even more so, are already happening—in all corners of the world, from the most pristine to the little corner you care about. We have not changed just one bay, we have changed the whole ocean on a global level.”
The new study, also authored by researchers at the U.K.’s Plymouth Marine Laboratory and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), finds that by 2020 the world’s oceans were already very close to the “danger zone” for ocean acidity, and in some regions had already crossed into it.

The new report puts the figure at about 17 percent.
“Ocean acidification isn’t just an environmental crisis, it’s a ticking time bomb for marine ecosystems and coastal economies,” said Steve Widdicombe, director of science at the Plymouth lab, in a press release. “As our seas increase in acidity, we’re witnessing the loss of critical habitats that countless marine species depend on and this, in turn, has major societal and economic implications.”
Scientists have determined that there are nine planetary boundaries that, once breached, risk humans’ abilities to live and thrive. One of these is climate change itself, which scientists have said is already beyond humanity’s “safe operating space” because of the continued emissions of heat-trapping gases. Another is ocean acidification, also caused by burning fossil fuels.
In 2023,
researchers determined
that six of these boundaries had already been crossed. The new research adds a worrying seventh.
The study, which was based on measurements from ice cores and data models, found that the acidity of the ocean was worse in deeper waters. At about 200 meters below the ocean’s surface, 60 percent of the ocean’s waters had already crossed the 20-percent threshold, compared to about 40 percent at the ocean’s surface.
“Most ocean life doesn’t just live at the surface—the waters below are home to many more different types of plants and animals,” said Helen Findlay, a biological oceanographer with the Plymouth lab and lead author of the new study “Since these deeper waters are changing so much, the impacts of ocean acidification could be far worse than we thought.”
The ocean’s increasing acidity has already led to tropical and subtropical reefs losing more than 40 percent of their habitats. data.title: Tell HN: Help restore the tax deduction for software dev in the US (Section 174)
data.author: dang
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Section 174 税法对软件工程师支出作为资本支出的税务处理及其对企业，特别是小型企业和初创企业的影响。

不同观点：
• **[支持修改税法观点]**：
  - **[rietta]**：作为小型企业主，Section 174 的修改对企业造成了严重的现金流压力。过去可以当年全额扣除的实验性开发支出，现在必须分五年摊销，导致即使没有盈利仍需缴税。这种情况限制了小型企业的创新能力，并可能迫使企业关闭。
  - **[jweir]**：小型软件企业联盟一直在努力推动这一问题的解决，认为该税法对创新企业不利，呼吁撤销这一修改。
  - **[vessenes]**：传统的资本资产处理方式不适用于所有软件开发，特别是那些需要快速迭代和创新的项目，现行税法对小型企业尤其不公平。

• **[对税法有保留的支持观点]**：
  - **[andrewlgood]**：作为前CFO，解释了FASB的会计规则如何驱动软件支出的资本化，指出税法与GAAP会计准则之间的联系。虽然理解资本化处理的初衷，但承认现行税法对小型企业造成了实际困难。
  - **[twodave]**：认为该税法对大企业的影响较小，但对小型企业和初创企业的影响较大，甚至可能导致小型企业倒闭，最终减少政府的税收。

• **[反对大企业税收优惠观点]**：
  - **[adamc]**：反对为大企业提供更多税收优惠，认为大企业长期以来已经获得过多税收优惠，当前应关注减少财政赤字，而非继续对大企业减税。

• **[质疑与策略讨论]**：
  - **[spruce_tips]**：提出企业是否可以通过改变工程师头衔来规避五年摊销限制，并对如何执行该税法提出疑问。
  - **[anigbrowl]**：回顾了该税法修改的初衷，指出其目的是为了将软件开发视为长期资产投资，但也承认这种处理方式在当前季度财报和短期收益为主的商业环境下并不合适。

• **[关于行动时机的讨论]**：
  - **[garrickvanburen]**：质疑为何在该法实施多年后才开始推动修改，并询问是什么改变了企业对这一问题的关注。
  - **[ryanisnan]**：询问是否会通过提交表格的方式代表签署者向相关委员会提交意见。

补充讨论：
• **具体例子与论据**：
  - **[mediaman]**：提供了详细的例子说明如何计算软件工程师支出的税务处理，指出该税法导致企业在支付高额薪水时只能部分扣除，增加了企业的税务负担。
  - **[jsherwani]**：用简单的例子说明了软件开发支出在税法修改前后的税务处理差异，强调了修改税法的重要性。

争议焦点：
• **现行税法是否合理**：支持修改者认为现行税法对小型企业和初创企业不公平，而反对者则认为大企业已经获得了足够的税收优惠，不应再受益。
• **如何有效推动税法修改**：讨论了推动修改税法的策略，包括通过联盟和政治游说等方式。

总的来说，评论主要集中在Section 174税法修改对小型企业和初创企业的负面影响，并呼吁通过各种途径推动税法修改。

data.title: Eleven studies by Spanish scientist Rafael Luque retracted due to fraud
data.author: belter
data.article_summary: 西班牙化学家拉斐尔·卢克（Rafael Luque）因频繁被引用而一度享有盛誉，但在2022年12月被科尔多瓦大学开除，11篇论文因欺诈行为被撤稿。他通过大量发表低质量论文迅速提升学术排名，特别是在泰国、沙特阿拉伯和西班牙等国家建立了广泛的合作网络。美国统计学家约翰·伊安尼迪斯发现，像卢克这样每年发表超过60篇论文的科学家数量显著增加。新工具Argos揭示，卢克的论文存在系统性操纵数据和买卖署名的问题，其行为涉及国际学术欺诈网络，影响了全球大学排名的真实性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科研产出的数量和质量

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：Mistletoe认为Luque的科研产出数量多得令人怀疑，强调每两个工作日发表一篇研究的速度是不正常的，隐含了对质量可能受到影响的担忧。
• 第二种观点：未直接引用，但可能存在的反驳观点是，高产出不一定意味着质量低。有些研究人员可能具备高效工作的能力，或者有大型研究团队的支持，使得高产出成为可能。

补充讨论：
• 有人可能会关注科研评价体系，认为当前学术界对数量的重视可能导致学者追求发表数量而忽视研究深度。
• 另一个讨论点是，不同学科的研究产出速度可能不同，某些领域如生物信息学或计算机科学可能更容易实现快速发表。
• 例子：Luque在2022年每两个工作日发表一篇研究，这一具体数据被用来支持其产出过高的观点。
• 争议的焦点在于高产出是否必然意味着质量下降，以及如何在数量和质量之间取得平衡。

The Spanish chemist Rafael Luque, 46, strode briskly onto the stage of the State Kremlin Palace in Moscow three months ago. In the
official video
, he appears ecstatic. He was about to receive a tribute for being one of the most frequently cited scientists in the world and having contributed, through his work, to the meteoric rise of the Peoples’ Friendship University of Russia
in the rankings of the world’s top academic institutions
.
The gala — a show with dancers and even a military choir — was reminiscent of Luque’s glory days back home, when he was receiving applause in the Spanish media and winning international awards. Back then, he seemed like a world authority, but the truth is that he was simply flouting the rules of the system using the same crude strategy that thousands of other researchers around the world were simultaneously implementing.
On December 1, 2022, Luque
was expelled from his university
, Universidad de Córdoba, with a historic sanction. A new tool now exposes how he rose to the top and how he fell, eventually becoming honored in the Kremlin as “pro-Russian.” Eleven studies of his have already been retracted for fraudulent practices.
Luque, born in the Andalusian city of Córdoba, is suspiciously prolific. He published a study every two working days in 2022. Then he actually accelerated his pace in December of that year, when the artificial intelligence language generation program
ChatGPT was released
. “These months have been quite productive, because the truth is that articles that used to take me two or three days to complete are now done in one day,” he acknowledged in a video call with EL PAÍS in March 2023, from a kitschy hotel in Dhahran, the headquarters of the Saudi oil industry. This newspaper has tried to speak with him again over the last month, but received no response. Luque’s work is focused on the so-called green chemistry, which attempts to synthesize products, such as pharmaceuticals and fuels, while generating less waste.
Publishing insubstantial studies
like hotcakes is one of the tricks used to climb the academic rankings.
An analysis
by U.S. statistician John Ioannidis last year identified some 3,200 scientists — 23 of them in Spain, including Luque — who publish more than 60 papers annually: at least one every five days. The number of hyperprolific researchers has increased most notably in three countries: Thailand (up nineteenfold in seven years), Saudi Arabia (up elevenfold), and Spain (up elevenfold). They also increased significantly in India (up tenfold), Russia (up sixfold), and Pakistan (up sixfold). Precisely in these countries, Luque wove a gigantic network of hundreds of collaborators, which facilitated his publication of ever more studies, which in turn were highly cited by those same colleagues. Thus, in 2018, he entered the prestigious
List of Highly Cited Researchers
, compiled by the multinational Clarivate.
The Spaniard is on his way to becoming one of the world’s researchers with the most studies retracted for fraudulent practices, according to data from
Argos
, a new tool for monitoring scientific integrity. His first work to be removed was an article on the synthesis of chemical compounds with supposed medical applications, which he co-authored with three researchers from Pakistan, two from China, and three from Saudi Arabia.
The publisher Wiley, after noting the “systematic manipulation” of the results, withdrew it on July 19, 2023. In October 2024 another publishing house, Elsevier, retracted four of his studies in one go after discovering “suspicious changes” in the authors’ names, which suddenly included the addition of Chinese, Korean, Pakistani and Taiwanese scientists — a common practice when authorship is sold to the highest bidder for a few hundred dollars, to pad their resumes without actually doing anything. His eleventh retraction
took place
three months ago, just days before his tribute at the Kremlin. It was a paper on chemical reaction catalysts, led by an Iranian scientist. Elsevier removed it after detecting “data manipulation.”
The Argos tool analyzes 57 million scientific studies every day in search of evidence of fraudulent practices. It was designed by
Scitility
, a public-benefit corporation created a year ago by Spanish computer scientist Antonio José Molina, his Dutch colleague Jan-Erik de Boer, and U.S. mathematician Gary Cornell. data.title: Private-Equity Billionaires Killed the American Dream
data.author: stevenwoo
data.article_summary:
梅根·格林威尔（Megan Greenwell）曾是体育博客Deadspin的总编辑，她在离职当天发表了一篇激烈批评其新东家——私募股权公司Great Hill Partners的文章，指责其不断削弱Deadspin的团队，追求快速套现。她指出，整个媒体行业越来越多地被私募股权公司和富豪控制，这些富人认为自己的财富等同于智慧，导致行业和员工深受其害。

格林威尔之后深入研究私募股权行业，并将其发现写成了一本书《Bad Company: Private Equity and the Death of the American Dream》。书中通过四个真实人物的故事，展示了私募股权公司如何通过巨额债务压垮企业，同时自身获利。这些人物包括玩具反斗城的一名主管、一名乡村医生、一名地方记者和一名保障性住房组织者，他们都在私募股权进入生活后受到影响，并试图反抗这一模式。

格林威尔强调，她希望通过展示私募股权对普通人生活的影响，让读者关注这个重要但可能枯燥的话题，并揭示该行业在追求利润的过程中如何影响整个社会。书中还探讨了私募股权公司与社区利益之间的脱节，指出杠杆收购是私募股权常用的策略，但往往只服务于公司自身利益，而非所收购企业的社区。

In the canon of spectacular resignations,
Megan Greenwell
’s is up there.
On her last day as editor in chief of the beloved sports blog
Deadspin,
Greenwell published
a blistering essay on the site about her soon-to-be former bosses at the private-equity firm Great Hill Partners, which had acquired
Deadspin
and other former Gawker properties earlier in 2019. In the essay, Greenwell accused Great Hill of undermining
Deadspin
’s staff at every turn and seeking a “quick cash-out” on its investment.
And it wasn’t just happening at
Deadspin,
Greenwell explained: “A metastasizing swath of media is controlled by private-equity vultures and capricious billionaires and other people who genuinely believe that they are rich because they are smart and that they are smart because they are rich, and that anyone less rich is by definition less smart.”
She’d written the post mostly for her own catharsis, Greenwell told
Vanity Fair.
But the response to it stunned her, as more than 1,000 messages poured in, many of them from readers who shared their own stories of how the private-equity industry had, in various ways, upended their lives too.
“It made me obsessive about reading about this, because I wanted to understand what had happened to me and to my coworkers and to my friends, and I realized that the only way to do that was by treating this as a reporting project,” Greenwell said.
Nearly six years later, Greenwell has funneled what she learned into a new book,
Bad Company: Private Equity and the Death of the American Dream.
The book is a deeply human account of the ways in which the multitrillion-dollar private-equity industry affected four different people: a Toys“R”Us supervisor who was laid off alongside the company’s 33,000 employees after the company declared bankruptcy following a private-equity acquisition; a rural doctor who watched private-equity ownership strip his Wyoming hospital of crucial services; a local reporter who helped lead union negotiations as private-equity-owned Gannett gutted newsrooms across the country; and an affordable-housing organizer whose own family suffered under a private-equity-industry landlord.
The book follows how private-equity firms like KKR, Bain Capital, Apollo Global Management, and more saddle the companies they acquire with insurmountable debt, even as the firms themselves profit. It also explores how each character in the book is fighting back against this model.
While
Bad Company
articulates how the industry works, its greater goal is to illustrate how the decisions the industry makes in the pursuit of profit influence us all. Greenwell spoke to
Vanity Fair
about who gets rich in private-equity takeovers, who gets hurt, and why no one in Washington seems willing to do much about it.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.
Vanity Fair:
I was grateful to you for writing a book about finance that doesn’t read like a book about finance. It’s about four people before, during, and after private equity came into their lives. Why did you want to structure it that way?
Megan Greenwell:
It was really important to show what came before private equity, because I think there’s an unfair line of critique that really blames them for everything. In the industries I focus on—retail, housing, health care, and local media—private equity didn’t create the problem. It’s important to draw that out and talk about the mistakes that those industry leaders made that ushered private equity in the door. On the other end, I felt like it was incredibly important to show efforts to build something new. I am not an activist. I did not want to write a prescriptive book, but I also didn’t want to write a book that was like: Man, this all sucks.
Why did you decide to ground it in the stories of these people?
I really love books that go deeply inside a company.
When McKinsey Comes to Town
was such a brilliant business book. It is also just
so
not the type of reporter I am. I am not, ultimately, that compelled in my own work by getting inside a glass skyscraper and showing how decisions are made. What is most compelling to me is the effect on real people. I thought that was the only way I could not only get readers compelled by this sometimes dull but important topic, but also excite myself about it.
In terms of potential characters, I would say I talked to over 150 people in these four industries. So I was incredibly picky, because I knew that if readers weren’t compelled by these people themselves, then they weren’t going to hang with the book.
The central tension of the book is about the disconnect between what serves private-equity firms and what serves the communities that surround the businesses they buy. I’d love you to spell out how that disconnect manifests.
Leveraged buyouts are a huge percentage of what private equity does. The basic way leveraged buyouts work is that the private-equity firm bundles together money from their outside investo

主要讨论点：多个平台同时出现宕机事件，是否存在关联

不同观点：
• 一方认为不同平台的宕机事件可能存在关联，并提出是否是更广泛的技术问题导致多个服务同时出现故障。例如，ChatGPT和Notion在相近时间段内出现宕机，这可能并非偶然，可能存在共同的基础设施或外部因素（如网络问题）影响了它们。
• 另一方则持怀疑态度，认为每个平台的宕机可能是独立事件，并没有明确的证据显示它们之间存在直接关联。这种观点指出，各个平台的技术架构和运营环境不同，宕机原因可能各异，因此不能轻易假设它们之间有共同的原因。

补充讨论：
• 有人提到需要进一步调查宕机时间的具体细节，确认这些事件是否真正同时发生或有重叠，从而判断是否存在潜在的关联。
• 宕机是否由外部因素（如云服务供应商的问题）引发，也被认为是值得探讨的方向，特别是如果多个平台依赖于同一云服务提供商。
• 争议的焦点在于是否存在共同的技术故障或外部影响导致了多个平台同时出现宕机，或者这些宕机事件仅仅是独立的技术问题。

data.title: Show HN: I made a 3D printed VTOL drone
data.author: tsungxu
data.article_summary: Tsung Xu在2025年6月10日发布文章，介绍他自制的3D打印垂直起降（VTOL）无人机，该无人机能够飞行130英里，持续飞行3小时，可能是世界上飞行距离和续航时间最长的3D打印VTOL无人机之一。Tsung在此项目之前几乎没有CAD、3D打印或空气动力学建模的经验，且仅在一个月前才开始使用3D打印机。他用了90天完成该项目，尽管视频因后期制作限制未能详细展示所有挑战和细节，但他表示如有兴趣可以提供更多设计和建造过程的信息。Tsung对该成果感到非常自豪，尤其是获得了Reid Hoffman的关注和转发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一项业余成就的技术分析和评价

不同观点：
• [asadm] 对项目印象深刻，关注其物料清单（BOM）和成本，特别提到电池可能是最昂贵的部分。
• [bufferoverflow] 认为该设计对于业余项目来说非常出色，但对垂直和水平飞行使用独立电机的方式提出质疑，指出这种设计会导致水平飞行时的效率低下和阻力增加，尽管承认增加旋转机构可能会增加重量。
• [georgel] 对项目表示赞赏，关注无人机的载重能力，询问其在自身重量之外还能承载多少有效载荷。
• [truetraveller] 对项目表示兴趣，但更关注无人机的最高速度。

补充讨论：
• 关于无人机设计中的效率问题存在一定争议，[bufferoverflow] 指出垂直电机在水平飞行中产生的阻力可能影响效率，但同时也承认改进设计会增加重量。
• 评论中涉及到对无人机不同性能指标的关注，包括成本、载重能力和速度，反映了不同用户对技术项目的不同兴趣点。
• 尽管存在一些技术上的争议，所有评论都对该业余成就表示了肯定和赞赏。

I made this 130 mile capable VTOL drone in only 90 days. It can fly for 3 hours on a single charge. That would make it one of the longest range and endurance 3D printed VTOLs in the world.
This is the thing I'm most proud of building to date!
Before this project, I was a total CAD, 3D printing and aerodynamic modeling beginner. I had only
built and flown one VTOL before
. My CAD skills were restricted to extrusions of basic sketches. My Bambu A1 3D printer was only one month old, and I had never tried printing foaming PLA. I had never used any aerodynamic modeling tools to simulate lift-to-drag ratios or stability curves like Cm-alpha.
This video edit ended up shorter than I planned. Being my first Youtube video with significant post production effort, I underestimated the work required to make a longer in-depth video with voiceover, edited footage, etc.
Because of that, I did not discuss dozens of project challenges like how I chose the design parameters, learnt airframe CAD design, sourced components, improved foaming PLA print quality, in-depth power loss troubleshooting, and many more challenges this project faced.
If you want more details on my design and build process, let me know!
P.S. Reid Hoffman just
quote tweeted
my viral
video post on X
:
A century ago, you needed at least a brother and a bicycle shop to pioneer flight. Today, you just need the right toolchain…
Incredibly humbling!

data.title: Xeneva Operating System
data.author: psnehanshu
data.article_summary: XenevaOS 是一个从头构建的操作系统，支持 x86_64 和 ARM64 架构。其内核名为 "Aurora"，采用混合内核设计，整个系统称为 "Xeneva"。该系统具有多种功能，包括 ACPI 支持、x64 和 ARM64 内核、高半内存、驱动加载、SSE/SSE3、USB3、Intel 高清音频、多处理器支持等。它还包括一个名为 "Deodhai" 的合成窗口管理器，一个名为 "Chitralekha" 的图形库，以及一个支持基本 ANSI/VT100 转义序列的终端。此外，Xeneva 还提供音频服务器、网络支持以及多种应用程序和驱动。该项目欢迎开发者贡献代码、文档、错误报告和功能建议，并且主要在 Windows 环境下构建。

XenevaOS
Xeneva is an operating system for both x86_64 and ARM64  architectures, built from the ground up. The Kernel is known as
'Aurora'
with hybrid kernel design and the entire operating system is known as
'Xeneva'
.
Please visit
Build Instructions
to build the project
Documentation
Refer to
Documentations of XenevaOS
Contributing to the project
XenevaOS is an open-source project that welcomes contributions from developers, researchers, and enthusiasts who are passionate about low level system development. Whether you're intereseted in Kernel development, driver development, low level graphics or application level features there are many ways to get involved. We encourage contibutions in the form of code, documentation, bug reports, and feature suggestions. If you're interested in contibuting, check out out
Contribution Guideline
, explore open issues, and join the discussion to help shape the project.
Features
:
ACPI (through acpica)
x64 and arm64 Kernel
Fully Higher Half Memory with MMIO mappings
Driver
loading and linking
through dll files
SSE/SSE3
USB3
Intel High Definition Audio
Multiprocessor support (muliprocessor scheduler not ready !!)
Application loader and dynamic library (shared library)
Freetype2 as font rendering engine
Compositing Window Manager called "Deodhai"
Graphics Library known as "Chitralekha"
Xeneva Terminal with basic ANSI/VT100 escape sequence support
Desktop environment called Namdapha Desktop
Storage supports : AHCI/SATA, NVMe
USB3 Class drivers (USB HID Mouse, USB Tablet, USB MSC driver) ..etc
Audio Server called "Deodhai-Audio" with
(44kHz/16bit audio format, stereo/mono panning, gain control)
Networking (IPv4, UDP/IP, TCP/IP, ICMP)
And many more coming soon

data.title: Low-background Steel: content without AI contamination
data.author: jgrahamc
data.article_summary: 该网站（lowbackgroundsteel.ai）创建于2023年3月，旨在汇集未受AI生成内容影响的在线资源。其名称“Low-background Steel”借用了一种未被核试验放射性同位素污染的金属概念，通常从1945年 Trinity Test 前沉没的船只中回收。网站聚焦于2022年AI生成内容爆发前创建的“未污染”文本、图像和视频资源，如ChatGPT发布前的维基百科备份、北极代码库和古登堡计划等。网站鼓励用户提交其他未受污染的资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容对训练数据的影响及可能的应对策略

不同观点：
• Legend2440认为，长期来看，AI应通过实际经验（如修车）而非阅读手册来学习，这样既能获取无限的非版权训练数据，也能避免AI污染问题。
• ACCount36指出，目前没有证据表明"AI污染"对训练有实际影响，且新旧数据训练出的AI性能差异不明显，有时新数据表现更好。
• gorgoiler乐观地认为，递归训练混合了人类原创内容和AI生成内容的数据，能够提取有用的特征和模式。
• Ekaros认为，经过筛选的、去除了低质量内容的训练数据可能更好，但同时也承认即使在AI之前，网络上也存在大量低质量内容。
• yodon怀疑人们对AI生成内容的识别能力，认为如果这种能力可靠，应该有商业价值。
• andy99指出，互联网上已有大量AI生成的垃圾内容，但他也提到过去也存在大量SEO和博客垃圾内容，训练方法可能已经对此具有抵抗力。

补充讨论：
• schmookeeg赞赏Legend2440将AI污染比作低背景钢，认为这是一个聪明的类比。
• vunderba质疑是否故意使用明显的AI生成图像作为横幅。
• nialv7质疑低背景钢的类比，认为不使用AI生成内容并不困难。
• aunty_helen提到通过检查用户资料创建时间来判断内容质量，但常常判断错误。
• sorokod提议为未污染内容设立"100%有机数据"标签和标志。
• mclau157认为这类似于archive.org的功能。
• swyx提供了一个AI污染网络的目录链接，并认为普通人对AI生成内容的接受度或无视度可能表明一定程度的噪音是无害的。

争议焦点：
• AI污染是否对训练数据构成实际威胁，以及是否需要采取措施来确保训练数据的质量。

44239481.article_content:
Somehow I forgot to blog my site:
https://lowbackgroundsteel.ai/
. I created it back in March 2023 as a clearinghouse for online resources that hadn't been contaminated with AI-generated content.
Low-background Steel
(and lead) is a type of metal uncontaminated by radioactive isotopes from nuclear testing. That steel and lead is usually recovered from ships that sunk before the Trinity Test in 1945. The site is about uncontaminated content that I'm terming "Low-background Steel". The idea is to point to sources of text, images and video that were created prior to the explosion of AI-generated content that occurred in 2022.
It currently contains pointers to a Wikipedia dump from prior to the release of ChatGPT, the Arctic Code Vault, Project Gutenberg, and more.
If you know of other sources of non-contaminated content plus
submit them
!

data.title: Mikeal Rogers has died
data.author: neom
data.article_summary: 这篇文章悼念了作者最好的朋友和同事Mikeal Rogers，他因侵袭性癌症去世。Mikeal是Node.js社区的核心人物，以其技术 brilliance 和人性光辉影响了无数人。他通过开放源代码的承诺，帮助和激励他人，无论是在深夜讨论策略，还是在支持年轻工程师方面。他坚信脆弱与严谨是相辅相成的，成功若缺乏同理心便毫无意义。他的离世让作者深感悲痛，但作者誓言将继续遵循他生前的原则：无 ego 的好奇心、无限制的慷慨和无门卫的社区。作者将铭记Mikeal的精神，继续前行。

44236728.article_content:
Mikeal Rogers, my best friend, my colleague, confidant, and one of a kind partner in countless late night chats and restless travel sprints, has died.
Mikeal died of aggressive cancer.
Words feel wholly inadequate because I want to capture the sweep of what he meant to me and to the many communities he shaped. Mikeal was core to nodejs, from our earliest days at DigitalOcean, when he turned developer evangelism into an act of radical hospitality, late night strategy sessions where we mapped new ideas on  napkins,  quiet moments where I cried over the weight of life, Mikeal modeled a rare combination of technical brilliance, clarity, and unfiltered humanity, reminding everyone in his orbit that code is just a conduit for connection for humans, for community. Mikel approached every project with the conviction that open source is not a license but a promise to lift others, and he lived that promise whether arguing a stubborn point at 3 a.m. or sitting with a junior engineer who doubted their place in tech. My growth traces directly to his insistence that vulnerability and rigor are not opposites but allies, that a great team is forged as much in shared laughter as in polish, that success is hollow if it leaves no room for empathy and compassion.
The grief of losing him is heavy, however even now I can hear his voice "Well John, you see..." urging us to keep building spaces where people feel seen and ideas flow freely.  I will carry forward that charge, honoring his memory by doubling down on the principles he lived every day:
curiosity without ego,
generosity without limit,
community without gatekeepers.
My dear dear friend, you saved my life and now I say: rest well, Mikeal, the paths we walked together remain lit by the fires you struck, those of us who traveled with you will keep the flame alive.
I will miss you Mikeal.

data.title: Another Crack in the Chain of Trust: Uncovering (Yet Another) Secure Boot Bypass
data.author: vitplister
data.article_summary: Binarly Research团队发现了一个影响大多数支持UEFI设备的Secure Boot bypass漏洞，编号为CVE-2025-3052。该漏洞源于一个使用微软第三方UEFI证书签名的模块，攻击者可利用其内存损坏漏洞在启动过程中运行未签名代码，从而绕过Secure Boot，危害系统信任链。漏洞的根本原因是不安全处理NVRAM变量，导致任意内存写入。微软在2025年6月10日的Patch Tuesday中通过向dbx数据库添加14个新哈希来缓解此问题。Secure Boot通过验证操作系统加载器的完整性和真实性来防止此类攻击，但此漏洞使其失效，可能导致早期攻击和系统防御被破坏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对某个与安全相关的补丁或漏洞（可能与NVRAM变量的不安全处理有关）的技术分析和责任归因。

不同观点：
• **lipowitz的观点**：  
  - 对“补丁星期二”发布的内容提出质疑，尤其关注是否真的解除了对某个禁令（可能与启动时的签名撤销有关）的限制。  
  - 论据：认为撤销一个启动时签名在技术上非常困难，尤其是在系统已经被入侵的情况下，仅仅通过操作系统启动来解决是不可能的。

• **db48x的观点**：  
  - 认为问题的根本原因是不安全处理NVRAM变量，并将其归因于纯粹的技术 incompetence（无能）。  
  - 论据：直指技术操作上的不专业或疏忽是问题的根源，暗示可能存在开发或维护上的失误。

- **争议焦点**：  
  1. 技术实施的难度，尤其是关于签名撤销在已经被入侵的系统上的可行性。  
  2. 对问题责任的归因：lipowitz没有明确责任方，而db48x则直接将问题归咎于技术 incompetence。
  
- **讨论关系**：  
  lipowitz的评论更偏向技术可行性和实际操作上的质疑，而db48x则从根本原因和责任归属上进行批评，二者形成了一种从技术细节到责任归属的讨论链条。

44240770.article_content:
Free scan
Book a demo
×
June 10, 2025
Another Crack in the Chain of Trust: Uncovering (Yet Another) Secure Boot Bypass
By Binarly REsearch
In this blog post, the Binarly Research team documents a Secure Boot bypass that likely impacts most devices supporting UEFI. At the center of this discovery is
CVE-2025-3052 (BRLY-2025-001)
, a memory corruption vulnerability in a module signed with Microsoftâs third-party UEFI certificate. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to run unsigned code during the boot process, effectively bypassing Secure Boot and compromising the systemâs chain of trust. Because the attackerâs code executes before the operating system even loads, it opens the door for attackers to install bootkits and undermine OS-level security defenses.
The story behind this discovery begins with a UEFI application we found on VirusTotal, signed with Microsoftâs third-party UEFI certificate. This application has been publicly available since November 2024 when it was first submitted. However, the signature data indicates it was actually signed in October 2022, suggesting it may have been circulating for much longer.
The application is a BIOS flashing tool for devices sold by DT Research, a company specializing in rugged mobile devices. Although this module was originally developed for DT Research devices only, it can run on any device that trusts the certificate with subject "
Microsoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011
" certificate. This includes the vast majority of systems, as the same certificate is widely used to sign the Linux bootloader shim, significantly increasing the potential impact of this vulnerability.
Figure 1. The vulnerable module signed with the Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 certificate
The root cause of this bug, once again, lies in the unsafe handling of NVRAM variables. Issues involving NVRAM variables have been a persistent problem in the UEFI ecosystem,
with Binarly alone responsibly disclosing hundreds of related vulnerabilities
over the past few years. Because these bugs have been so widespread and impactful, our Binarly Transparency Platform performs multiple analyses to detect these bug classes. One of these checks looks specifically for any unsafe usage of data read from NVRAM variables, and this analysis is what automatically discovered CVE-2025-3052.
As shown in the image below, the signed application reads the content of the
IhisiParamBuffer
variable and directly uses it as a pointer for multiple memory write operations, without performing any validation or sanity checks on its value. This allows an attacker to set the
IhisiParamBuffer
variable to any arbitrary address in memory, effectively granting them an arbitrary memory write primitive.
Figure 2. The signed module blindly trusting an NVRAM variable for memory writes Â (CVE-2025-3052)
We reported this finding to CERT/CC on February 26, 2025. During our disclosure with Microsoft, it became clear that this issue wasnât limited to a single module, but it actually affected 14 different modules. For this reason, to address CVE-2025-3052, Microsoft added 14 new hashes to the Secure Boot dbx as a mitigation measure, which was delivered as part of Patch Tuesday on June 10, 2025.
Secure Boot and Microsoft Certificates
Before delving into the details of CVE-2025-3052, letâs recap what Secure Boot is and what security problems it solves. First of all, Secure Boot plays a crucial role in the chain of trust built by UEFI. It can be thought of as a bridge connecting the systemâs firmware to the operating system, carrying trust from one bank to the other. At the end of the DXE phase, with the platform initialized, the firmware is ready to boot the OS. With Secure Boot, the firmware cryptographically verifies the integrity and authenticity of the OS loader before handing over control. This check stops attackers from replacing the legitimate OS loader with a malicious component, such as a bootkit. Without Secure Boot, it is trivial for attackers to gain early execution, compromising OS defenses before the OS even has a chance to install them.
Figure 3. Summary of the UEFI Secure Boot signing and verification process
UEFI applications are signed with the private part of a signing certificate (leaf certificate on the image) that chains through one or more intermediate certificates to a trusted, root CA certificate from
db
. This is for example what happens with applications signed by Microsoft, where the private key of the certificate with subject âMicrosoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011â signs the signing/leaf certificate, whose private key is in turn used to sign the Authentocode hash of the UEFI Application.
The verification process is instead based on two signature databases:
db
and
dbx
. The
db
contains a list of trusted Authenticode hashes and root certificates:
if any Authenticode hash in the
db
matches the applicationâs Authenticode hash, the application is allowed to run
if any root certificate in the
db
successfully verifies

主要讨论点：不同用户对GPT及相关模型（如o3、o3-pro、o4等）性能、价格和实用性的评价和讨论。

不同观点：
• DanMcInerney：希望GPT5在性能指标上有显著提升，尽管基准测试显示改进不大，但在实际任务中，新一代模型感觉更好。他还建议是否可以有专门针对任务导向数据进行训练的模型，通过微调或强化学习来提高任务分解和实施的能力。
• Chad1n：质疑o3-pro是否只是o3的量化版本，并希望有人能对这些模型进行基准测试以检查质量是否下降。
• WhitneyLand：认为o3已经是非常强大的模型，甚至优于Anthropic 4和Gemini 2.5，尤其在工具使用方面表现突出。尽管成本较高，但在前沿领域有其价值。
• Manmal：指出基准测试显示o3-pro相对o3提升不大，质疑是否性能提升正在趋缓，接近收益递减点。
• Swyx：引用用户评价，强调o3-pro提供了具体且扎实的计划，改变了团队对未来的思考方式，显示出其在实际应用中的价值。

补充讨论：
• Tiahura：简单询问是否值得升级到Teams并支付50美元。
• ChrisArchitect：提到OpenAI将o3的价格下调了80%，并提供相关新闻链接。
• Carmelion：仅简短提到Jl App，未展开具体观点。
• Mmsc：认为目前提供的8个模型可能让用户感到困惑，质疑是否有必要提供如此多的选择。
• Cluckindan：对“设计为更长时间思考”持怀疑态度，认为这可能只是为了让人们相信模型在更深入思考。

争议焦点：
• 模型性能的实际提升幅度，特别是o3和o3-pro之间的差异，以及是否正在接近性能提升的瓶颈。
• 多种模型并存是否导致用户选择困难，以及是否需要简化模型选择以提升用户体验。

General summary

Bullet points
"Android 16 is here!" This article highlights the newest Android release, rolling out to Pixel devices first.
Live updates from apps like food delivery will appear in notifications, and notifications from one app will be grouped.
Android 16 improves hearing aid compatibility, letting you use your phone's mic for clearer calls.
Advanced Protection gives you stronger security against online attacks, harmful apps, and scam calls.
Desktop windowing on tablets lets you open multiple app windows, like on a computer, for better productivity.
Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.
Basic explainer
Android 16 is here and it's got cool new stuff. You can see live updates for your food deliveries. It also makes calls easier for people with hearing aids. Plus, it has stronger security to keep your phone safe.
Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

Today, we’re bringing you Android 16, rolling out first to supported Pixel devices with more phone brands to come later this year. This is the
earliest
Android has launched a major release in the last few years, which ensures you get the latest updates as soon as possible on your devices.
Android 16 lays the foundation for our new
Material 3 Expressive
design, with features that make Android more accessible and easy to use. Let’s take a look at what’s new:
Streamlined and up-to-date notifications
Waiting for your food delivery to get to your house? Instead of opening your delivery app every 5 minutes, live updates keep you informed in real-time. These live updates are starting with compatible ride-share and food delivery apps. We’re working together with these app partners to bring this capability to the Android ecosystem, including in Samsung’s Now Bar and OPPO and OnePlus’ Live Alerts.
UI may vary
We’re also force-grouping notifications that come from a single app to help reduce information overload. Your notifications will automatically be grouped together to keep things looking tight and organized.
Clearer, simpler calling with hearing devices
Android 16 provides significant enhancements for people who use hearing aids
1
. Current LE audio hearing devices use their built-in front-facing mics for audio input. Those mics are designed to pick up the sound of the person you're speaking to — not the sound of your voice. Now you can switch to using your phone's microphone for clearer calls in noisy environments.
We’re also releasing native control for hearing devices in Android 16 for easier access and a more consistent experience. This means you can now control things like volume on your hearing devices right from your Android phone.
Stronger security in a single tap
With Android 16, you can now activate
Advanced Protection
2
, Google’s strongest mobile device protection. It enables an array of robust device security features that protect you from online attacks, harmful apps, unsafe websites, scam calls and more. Whether you’re a public figure or you just prioritize security, Advanced Protection gives you greater peace of mind that you’re protected against the most sophisticated attacks.
Enhanced productivity for tablets
Samsung
DeX
has helped maximize productivity on phones, foldables and tablets for years. In Android 16, we worked closely with Samsung to develop desktop windowing, a new way to interact with your apps and content on large-screen devices. In addition to the single app and split-screen modes, you can open, move and resize multiple app windows in a single screen, just like a desktop. This makes it easier to work across apps. Android 16’s desktop windowing will roll out later this year on compatible devices.
Later this year, we’re also launching custom keyboard shortcuts, so you can create your own combination of hotkeys, and taskbar overflow, which provides a simple, visual way for you to find the app you need when the taskbar is full. Future updates will also bring even more productivity enhancements to Android, allowing you to connect tablets and phones to an external display for an expanded desktop experience, and
developers can begin testing

data.title: A Family of Non-Periodic Tilings, Describable Using Elementary Tools
data.author: joshu
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种使用基本工具（如模算术和向量几何）构造的非周期性铺砖方法。这些铺砖展示了一种新的结构规律性，称为模错列旋转对称。该构造独立于先前的铺砖理论，包含12张图示和13页内容，提交至组合数学领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一种新型非周期性瓷砖形状的潜在应用和数学描述的讨论

不同观点：
• **jameshart的观点**：这种新型的数学瓷砖形状具有很高的美学价值，尤其是其独特的形状。jameshart认为，这类形状应该被瓷砖或铺路砖制造商采用，因为它们在视觉上非常吸引人，且不同于传统的六边形瓷砖。他强调了这种形状的实际应用潜力，特别是在建筑和设计领域。

• **joshu的观点**：joshu提供了关于该形状的更多技术细节，指出这种形状属于一种“非周期性镶嵌”，可以用基础工具描述，并展现出一种新型的结构规律性。joshu还指出了该形状与Miki Imura的螺旋镶嵌的关系，表明其背后有着复杂的数学理论支持，而不仅仅是美学上的吸引力。joshu的观点更侧重于该形状在数学和理论上的重要性。

补充讨论：
• **实际应用 vs. 理论价值**：jameshart更关注这种形状在实际生活中的应用，如用于瓷砖或铺路砖，而joshu则更强调其在数学上的创新性和结构规律性。这反映了讨论中实际应用与理论研究之间的张力。

• **非周期性镶嵌的独特性**：joshu指出了这种形状的非周期性特点，这与传统的周期性镶嵌（如六边形）有显著不同，可能在数学和建筑设计中具有独特的应用价值。

争议焦点：目前讨论中没有明显的争议，但存在不同的关注点。jameshart关注实用性，而joshu则关注理论创新，两者都认可这种形状的价值，但侧重点不同。

Abstract:
We present a construction of a family of non-periodic tilings using elementary tools such as modular arithmetic and vector geometry. These tilings exhibit a distinct type of structural regularity, which we term modulo-staggered rotational symmetry. The construction is self-contained and does not rely on previous tiling theories or systems.

44240691.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种使用基本工具（如模算术和向量几何）构造的非周期性铺砖方法。这些铺砖展示了一种新的结构规律性，称为模错列旋转对称。该构造独立于先前的铺砖理论，包含12张图示和13页内容，提交至组合数学领域。
44240691.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一种新型非周期性瓷砖形状的潜在应用和数学描述的讨论

不同观点：
• **jameshart的观点**：这种新型的数学瓷砖形状具有很高的美学价值，尤其是其独特的形状。jameshart认为，这类形状应该被瓷砖或铺路砖制造商采用，因为它们在视觉上非常吸引人，且不同于传统的六边形瓷砖。他强调了这种形状的实际应用潜力，特别是在建筑和设计领域。

• **joshu的观点**：joshu提供了关于该形状的更多技术细节，指出这种形状属于一种“非周期性镶嵌”，可以用基础工具描述，并展现出一种新型的结构规律性。joshu还指出了该形状与Miki Imura的螺旋镶嵌的关系，表明其背后有着复杂的数学理论支持，而不仅仅是美学上的吸引力。joshu的观点更侧重于该形状在数学和理论上的重要性。

补充讨论：
• **实际应用 vs. 理论价值**：jameshart更关注这种形状在实际生活中的应用，如用于瓷砖或铺路砖，而joshu则更强调其在数学上的创新性和结构规律性。这反映了讨论中实际应用与理论研究之间的张力。

• **非周期性镶嵌的独特性**：joshu指出了这种形状的非周期性特点，这与传统的周期性镶嵌（如六边形）有显著不同，可能在数学和建筑设计中具有独特的应用价值。

争议焦点：目前讨论中没有明显的争议，但存在不同的关注点。jameshart关注实用性，而joshu则关注理论创新，两者都认可这种形状的价值，但侧重点不同。

data.title: Web-scraping AI bots cause disruption for scientific databases and journals
data.author: tchalla
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了网络爬虫机器人对科学数据库和期刊网站造成的干扰问题。这些自动化程序试图从网站上抓取大量内容，导致服务器过载，影响正常用户访问。特别是随着生成式人工智能（AI）工具的兴起，如聊天机器人和图像生成器，这类爬虫活动愈加猖獗。许多学术出版商和研究机构报告称，机器人流量已超过真实用户，导致服务中断和运营问题。例如，在线图像库DiscoverLife和医学期刊出版商BMJ都受到了影响。尽管开放获取的内容欢迎合理重用，但一些爬虫行为过于激进，给资源有限的组织带来了巨大压力。网站所有者正努力阻止这些机器人，但任务艰巨，亟需解决方案。

44241089.article_content:
Web-scraping AI bots cause disruption for scientific databases and journals
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook

You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
Some websites have been overwhelmed by the sheer volume of bot traffic.
Credit: Marco VDM/Getty
In February, the online image repository
DiscoverLife
, which contains nearly three million photographs of different species, started to receive millions of hits to its website every day — a much higher volume than normal. At times, this spike in traffic was so high that it
slowed the site down
to the point that it became unusable. The culprit? Bots.
These automated programs, which attempt to ‘scrape’ large amounts of content from websites, are increasingly becoming a headache for scholarly publishers and researchers who run sites hosting journal papers, databases and other resources.
Open-source AI chatbots are booming — what does this mean for researchers?
Much of the bot traffic comes from anonymized IP addresses, and the sudden increase has led many website owners to suspect that these web-scrapers are gathering data to train
generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools
such as chatbots and image generators.
“It’s the wild west at the moment,” says Andrew Pitts, the chief executive of PSI, a company based in Oxford, UK, that provides a global repository of validated IP addresses for the scholarly communications community. “The biggest issue is the sheer volume of requests” to access a website, “which is causing strain on their systems. It costs money and causes disruption to genuine users.”
Those that run affected sites are working on ways to block the bots and reduce the disruption they cause. But this is no easy task, especially for organizations with limited resources. “These smaller ventures could go extinct if these sorts of issues are not dealt with,” says Michael Orr, a zoologist at the Stuttgart State Museum of Natural History in Germany.
A flood of bots
Internet bots have been around for decades, and some have been useful. For example, Google and other search engines have bots that scan millions of web pages to identify and retrieve content. But the
rise of generative AI
has led to a deluge of bots, including many ‘bad’ ones that scrape without permission.
This year, the BMJ, a publisher of medical journals based in London, has
seen bot traffic to its websites surpass that of real users
. The aggressive behaviour of these bots overloaded the publisher’s servers and led to interruptions in services for legitimate customers, says Ian Mulvany, BMJ’s chief technology officer.
Social scientists battle bots to glean insights from online chatter
Other publishers report similar issues. “We’ve seen a huge increase in what we call ‘bad bot’ traffic,” says Jes Kainth, a service delivery director based in Brighton, UK, at Highwire Press, an Internet hosting service that specializes in scholarly publications. “It’s a big problem.”
The Confederation of Open Access Repositories (COAR)
reported in April
that more than 90% of 66 members it surveyed had experienced AI bots scraping content from their sites — of which roughly two-thirds had experienced service disruptions as a result. “Repositories are open access, so in a sense, we welcome the reuse of the contents,” says Kathleen Shearer, COAR’s executive director. “But some of these bots are super aggressive, and it’s leading to service outages and significant operational problems.”
Training data
One factor driving the rise in AI bots was a revelation that came with the
release of DeepSeek
, a Chinese-built large language model (LLM). Before that, most LLMs required a huge amount of computational power to create, explains Rohit Prajapati, a development and operations manager at Highwire Press. But the developers behind DeepSeek showed that an LLM that
rivals popular generative-AI tools
could be made with many fewer resources, kick-starting an explosion of bots seeking to scrape the data needed to train this type of model.

data.title: Apple announces Foundation Models and Containerization frameworks, etc
data.author: thm
data.article_summary: 苹果公司于2025年6月9日宣布了一系列新的开发者工具和技术，旨在帮助开发者在苹果平台上创建更美观、智能和互动的应用程序。新设计采用了名为“Liquid Glass”的材料，使应用更具表现力和愉悦感，同时保持熟悉度。Xcode 26集成大型语言模型（如ChatGPT），提供智能编码工具。新的Foundation Models框架让开发者能够利用设备上的智能模型，实现离线可用和保护隐私的AI功能，且支持Swift，仅需三行代码即可访问。Icon Composer应用帮助开发者设计视觉吸引力强的应用图标。这些新工具和增强功能旨在助力开发者快速、自信地构建现代化应用程序。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple 在 WWDC 2025 推出的新工具和框架，包括 Xcode 26 的新功能、AI 模型框架、容器化技术等。

不同观点：
• [gdubs] 认为 Xcode 26 的新功能，如生成式语言模型和 vibe-coding 集成，虽然不是完全开创性的，但提升了开发者的用户体验（UX）。他特别提到这些功能是本地运行，且与设备紧密集成。
• [pxc] 对容器化框架感到失望，原本期望 macOS 能原生支持 Linux 容器，但目前只能通过虚拟机实现。他认为 macOS 缺乏真正的原生容器支持，而第三方在没有苹果合作的情况下难以实现这一功能。
• [pzo] 指出，尽管新的 AI 模型框架很有趣，但它们仅支持 iPhone 15 Pro 和 iPhone 16 系列，覆盖面太小，对第三方开发者吸引力不足。
• [dedicate] 认为容器化框架是一个重要的改进，特别是如果它能简化 Linux 容器的使用，可能会改变开发者的工作流程。
• [chakintosh] 提到 iPadOS 和 macOS 正在逐渐融合，并预测除非有特殊需求，iPad 可能会取代大部分用户的笔记本电脑。
• [badc0ffee] 提供了关于容器化框架的技术细节，指出每个容器将在自己的虚拟机中运行，但没有透露更多技术细节。
• [guybedo] 总结了几点，包括 Apple 的 AI 模型减少了应用包大小和 API 调用，但容器化框架基于虚拟机，而非原生内核集成。
• [Illniyar] 对苹果采用类似 Windows Aero 的 UI 设计表示质疑，认为这种设计趋势可能不会持久。
• [KolibriFly] 对 Xcode 集成 ChatGPT 的实际效果持怀疑态度，指出苹果在开发者工具方面的历史表现不稳定。
• [mohsen1] 对 iPad 更新可能吸引更多开发者使用 iPad 编程表示谨慎乐观。

补充讨论：
• [runjake] 澄清了“Foundation Models”是 Apple 的一个新框架，集成了多种 Apple 的设备上 AI 模型。
• [nikolayasdf123] 提到一个关于 Apple 机器学习框架的旧问题，暗示某些技术问题可能尚未解决。
• [xpe] 对 Apple 提供的超过 250,000 个 API 表示惊讶，认为这听起来很疯狂。
• [dang] 提供了与其他讨论线程的链接，这些线程进一步讨论了 Apple 的容器化技术和 Linux 容器运行时。

争议焦点：
• 容器化框架是否真正满足开发者需求，特别是与第三方工具（如 OrbStack）相比。
• 新 AI 模型框架的设备支持范围有限，是否值得第三方开发者采用。
• Xcode 集成 ChatGPT 功能的实际效果和用户体验如何。

总的来说，讨论围绕 Apple 新推出的开发者工具和框架展开，涉及功能实用性、技术细节、用户体验和市场策略等多方面。

PRESS RELEASE
June 9, 2025
Apple supercharges its tools and technologies for developers to foster creativity, innovation, and design
Access to the on-device Apple Intelligence model, large language model integration in Xcode, and an elegant new software design across Apple platforms give developers everything they need to build beautiful modern apps with speed and confidence
Apple announced new technologies and enhancements to its developer tools to help developers create more beautiful, intelligent, and engaging app experiences across Apple platforms.
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA
Apple today announced new technologies and enhancements to its developer tools to help developers create more beautiful, intelligent, and engaging app experiences across Apple platforms. A beautiful new software design brings more focus to content, and delivers more expressive and delightful experiences across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26,
1
while keeping them all instantly familiar. The Foundation Models framework joins a suite of tools that allow developers to tap into on-device intelligence, and Xcode 26 leverages large language models like ChatGPT, giving them access to Xcode’s Coding Tools and other intelligent features.
These new resources join the extensive and continuously evolving set of technologies Apple offers developers, including over 250,000 APIs that enable developers to integrate their apps with Apple’s hardware and software features. These APIs span a wide range of capabilities, such as machine learning, augmented reality, health and fitness, spatial computing, and high-performance graphics. With each platform release, Apple expands and refines its technologies and tools to assist developers in bringing their ideas to life and delivering rich, responsive, and optimized experiences across Apple platforms.
“Developers play a vital role in shaping the experiences customers love across Apple platforms,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations. “With access to the on-device Apple Intelligence foundation model and new intelligence features in Xcode 26, we’re empowering developers to build richer, more intuitive apps for users everywhere.”
New Design with Liquid Glass
The elegant new design gives developers the opportunity to make their apps more expressive and delightful, while being instantly familiar. It’s crafted with a new software-based material called Liquid Glass, which combines the optical qualities of glass with a sense of fluidity. This gorgeous new material extends from the smallest elements users interact with every day — like buttons, switches, sliders, text, and media controls — to larger elements, including tab bars and sidebars for navigating apps.
The elegant new design, crafted with Liquid Glass, gives developers the opportunity to make their apps more expressive and delightful, while being instantly familiar.
Native frameworks like SwiftUI give developers everything they need to adopt the new design in their apps. The universal design allows developers to bring greater focus to their users’ content, establishing a consistent experience when developing across Apple’s platforms.
With the all-new Icon Composer app, developers and designers are empowered to create visually captivating app icons that enhance their app’s identity. This powerful tool helps create a consistent visual identity for app icons by annotating layers for multiple rendering modes, with advanced features that include blurring, adjusting translucency, testing specular highlights, and previewing icons in various tints.
With the all-new Icon Composer app, both developers and designers are empowered to create visually captivating app icons that enhance their app’s identity.
Foundation Models Framework
With the Foundation Models framework, developers will be able to build on Apple Intelligence to bring users new experiences that are intelligent, available when they’re offline, and that protect their privacy, using AI inference that is free of cost.
The framework has native support for Swift, so developers can easily access the Apple Intelligence model with as few as three lines of code. Guided generation, tool calling, and more are all built into the framework, making it easier than ever to implement generative capabilities right into an existing app. For example, Automattic is using the framework in its Day One journaling app to bring users privacy-centric intelligence features.
“The Foundation Model framework has helped us rethink what’s possible with journaling,” said Paul Mayne, head of Day One at Automattic. “Now we can bring intelligence and privacy together in ways that deeply respect our users.”

data.title: Go is a good fit for agents
data.author: abelanger
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何Go语言非常适合用于开发代理（agent）程序。代理通常是长时间运行的进程，具有较高的执行成本，并且常常等待I/O或用户输入。Go语言的并发模型非常适合这种场景，因为它的goroutine非常轻量，可以同时运行大量并发任务，而不会对系统造成过大负担。相比于Node.js或Python，Go在处理CPU密集型任务时表现更佳，因其利用多核CPU的能力更强。此外，Go编译成单一二进制文件，内存占用低，进一步提升了其在代理开发中的优势。总体而言，Go的高并发性、高效的I/O处理和低内存占用使其成为代理程序开发的理想选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：代理系统中的编程语言选择，特别是Python、Go和TypeScript等语言在代理系统中的适用性及其优缺点。

不同观点：
• [_QrE] 认为Python更适合用于代理系统，因为其在AI领域的库支持非常丰富。尽管执行速度可能比其他语言慢，但在大多数情况下，用户不会在意这一点。同时，他认为代理系统的延迟主要来自于LLM调用，而不是语言本身的执行速度。
• [jeswin] 支持TypeScript作为AI系统的粘合语言，认为其类型系统更具表现力和成熟度。虽然承认Python有广泛的库支持，但指出在取消长时运行任务方面，Python和Node.js都存在困难。
• [pantsforbirds] 提出Elixir和BEAM的组合可能是当前代理系统的最佳选择，因为其并发性和可扩展性非常好，并且可以轻松创建有状态或临时代理。他还计划使用MCP服务器支持多语言代理开发。
• [lunarcave] 认为代理系统大部分时间都在等待LLM响应和执行API调用，因此语言运行时的性能不太重要，JSON序列化和反序列化的性能反而是关键。
• [huqedato] 支持[pantsforbirds]的观点，认为Elixir是代理系统的理想选择。
• [flanked-evergl] 强烈批评Go的类型系统，认为其非常有限，使得Go在许多情况下不适合使用。
• [skybrian] 指出在长时运行过程中，如果进程被杀死，所有工作都会丢失，因此建议将状态序列化到数据库中，但这会增加复杂性。
• [odyssey7] 调侃AI工程师不会使用JavaScript，并提到TensorFlow转向Swift对AI语言多样性的影响。
• [guywithahat] 希望ML领域有更好的并发模型，指出Go在ML方面的库支持不足，而Python和C++也各有其缺点。
• [rgavuliak] 提到一个名为"Modern Data Science in Go"的演讲，认为其中的许多论点具有误导性。
• [InTheArena] 不认为Go适合LLM，并分享了从Go转向Swift的经历，发现Swift在代码生成方面表现更好。
• [jillesvangurk] 认为Go和其他许多语言一样，既不特别好也不特别差。他指出代理系统涉及大量状态管理和异步任务，因此可能需要外部化状态管理，并利用现有的中间件。
• [myzie] 支持原文观点，正在使用Go构建代理系统，认为Go在并发和扩展性方面有优势，但承认Go在ML库支持方面的不足。
• [carsoon] 分享了使用Go构建代理系统的经验，认为通过序列化和去耦合可以实现高效的代理工作流，但指出Go社区在这方面的开发者较少。
• [TeeWEE] 指出Go缺乏像Python那样的自动OpenAOI生成能力，需要依赖反射，不如Python方便。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于不同语言在代理系统中的适用性，特别是Python、Go和TypeScript。Python被广泛认可其库支持，但被批评在取消长时运行任务方面存在困难。Go的类型系统和并发模型受到批评，但其在并发和扩展性方面的优势也被认可。TypeScript的类型系统表现力和成熟度受到赞扬。
• 讨论中多次提到代理系统的性能瓶颈在于LLM调用和JSON序列化/反序列化，而非语言本身的执行速度。
• 有人提出外部化状态管理和利用中间件来解决长时运行代理系统的状态保持问题。

Why Go is a good fit for agents
Why Go is a good fit for agents
Since you’re here, you might be interested in checking out
Hatchet
— the platform for running background tasks, data pipelines and AI agents at scale.
Alexander Belanger
Published on June 3, 2025
Like seemingly everyone else on the planet, we’ve been spending the last few months fussing over agents.
In particular, we’ve been seeing the adoption of agents drive the growth of our orchestration platform, so we have some insight into what sorts of stacks and frameworks —
or lack thereof
— work well here.
One of the more interesting things we’ve seen is a proliferation of hybrid stacks: a typical Next.js or FastAPI backend, coupled with an
agent written in Go,
even at a very early stage.
As a long-time Go developer, this is rather exciting; here’s why I think this will be a more common approach moving forward.
What’s an agent?
Terminology here is muddled, but in general I’m referring to a process which is executing in a loop, where the process has some agency over the next step in its execution path. Contrast this with a predefined execution path, like a set of steps defined as a directed acyclic graph, which we’d call a
workflow
. Agents often contain an exit condition based on maximum depth or a condition (like “tests pass”) being met.
Source:
https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents
Agents typically have a number of shared characteristics when they start to scale (read:
have actual users
):
They are long-running — anywhere from seconds to minutes to hours.
Each execution is expensive — not just the LLM calls, but the nature of the agent is to replace something that would typically require a human operator. Development environments, browser infrastructure, large document processing — these all cost $$$.
They often involve input from a user (or another agent!) at some point in their execution cycle.
They spend a lot of time awaiting i/o or a human.
Let’s translate this set of characteristics into runtime. To constrain the problem, let’s assume that we’re dealing with an agent that is executed
remotely
and not on a user’s machine (though Go would be a great choice for distributing a local agent as well). In the case of remote execution, it would be incredibly expensive to run a separate container for each agent execution, so in most cases (particularly when our agent is simple i/o and LLM calls), we are going to end up with a bunch of lightweight processes that are running concurrently. Each process can be in a given state (for example, “Searching files,” “Generating code,” “Test”). Note that the ordering of states is not the same in for different agent executions.
This system of many concurrent, long-running processes is quite different from a traditional web architecture of ~10 years ago, where requests to a server were much faster, and thousands of daily users could be served efficiently using
some caches, efficient handlers and OLTP databases
.
It turns out, this shift in architecture is really well-suited to Go’s concurrency model, reliance on channels for communication, centralized cancellation mechanism, and tooling built around i/o.
High concurrency
Let’s start with the obvious — Go has an incredibly simple and powerful concurrency model. Spawning a new goroutine costs very little memory and time, as there’s only 2kb of pre-allocated memory per goroutine.
Source:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KBZlN0izeiY&t=586s
Effectively this means that you can run many goroutines at once with little overhead, and they run on
multiple OS threads
under the hood which take advantage of all CPU cores in your server. This is rather important, because if you
happen
to do something very CPU-intensive in a goroutine (like deserializing a large JSON payload), you will see less of an impact than if you were using a single-threaded runtime like Node.js (where you’d need to spawn out to a worker thread or child process for something that blocks the thread) or Python’s async/await.
What does this mean for agents? Because agents are longer-running than a typical web request, concurrency becomes a much greater point of concern. In Go, you’re much less likely to be constrained by spawning a goroutine per agent than if you ran a thread per agent in Python or an async function per agent in Node.js. Couple this with a lower baseline memory footprint and compilation into a single binary, and it becomes incredibl

data.title: Apple introduces a universal design across platforms
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 苹果公司于2025年6月9日推出全新软件设计，采用名为“Liquid Glass”的新材料，使应用程序和系统体验更具表现力和愉悦感。该设计在iOS 26、iPadOS 26、macOS Tahoe 26、watchOS 26和tvOS 26中实现跨平台统一，同时保持各平台独特性。Liquid Glass材料具有半透明特性，能根据内容和环境动态变化，提升用户对内容的关注度。新的设计包括重新设计的控件、工具栏和导航，适应圆角显示，并通过动态变化使用户更易于操作。系统体验如锁屏、主屏幕等也得到更新，旨在提供更和谐、直观的用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果新推出的半透明“液态玻璃”设计及其影响

不同观点：
• **反对新设计，关注可访问性问题**：
  - [dimal] 认为半透明设计会导致文本难以辨认，特别是对像他这样的自闭症患者不友好，并担心这会广泛影响其他用户。
  - [stalco] 实际安装后，认为设计过于繁杂，设置应用的比例不佳，且对可访问性是“地狱”般的体验。
  - [pardner] 批评新设计过于注重形式而非功能，认为苹果在解决技术债务问题之前不应该推出这种视觉更新。
  - [stevenhubertron] 同样认为新设计在可访问性和可用性上存在严重问题，并表示如果最终设计如此糟糕，可能会放弃使用苹果产品。

• **对新设计持保留态度，但理解其背后的动机**：
  - [designerarvid] 作为用户体验设计师，虽然不完全赞同新设计，但理解其可能是为了吸引年轻一代（尤其是GenZ）用户，并认为这种设计可能是为了传达“高级质量”。
  - [pentagrama] 虽然对新设计的动画效果表示担忧，认为可能导致分心，但也相信苹果会提供关闭选项，且理解这种设计可能是出于营销需求。

• **对新设计持积极态度，认为具有创新潜力**：
  - [captainmuon] 认为新设计利用了现代高分辨率显示器和强大GPU的优势，可以带来更具物理性和现实感的界面设计，只要开发者易于实现这种设计，它有可能成功。
  - [kylehotchkiss] 赞赏苹果在设计上的投入，认为尽管新设计不完美，但可以通过调整对比度来改善，并期待苹果未来在原生UI上的进一步优化。

• **对新设计持怀疑态度，担心历史重演**：
  - [kej] 认为新设计与微软Windows 8的“Metro”设计目标类似，担心苹果会在损害桌面体验的情况下推行这种设计。
  - [ricokatayama] 认为“液态玻璃”设计是苹果设计上的倒退，担心苹果进入“设计地狱”，难以回归简洁有效的设计。

• **历史对比与怀旧情绪**：
  - [StopDisinfo910] 表达了对新设计似曾相识的感觉，联想到早期的Windows Longhorn和Vista设计，认为这是旧设计的新生。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现与未来趋势**：
  - [nharada] 猜测半透明设计可能是为未来的AR界面做准备，因为AR眼镜无法完全显示不透明元素，这种设计可以确保跨平台的一致性。

• **设计历史与影响**：
  - [gherkinnn] 引用了一篇博客，指出新设计与早期Longhorn（后来的Vista）设计相似，表明这种设计趋势早有预测。

争议焦点：
• 新设计的可访问性和可用性问题，特别是对特殊群体（如自闭症患者）的影响。
• 新设计是否过于注重视觉效果而忽视功能性和效率。
• 新设计是否预示着未来AR界面的发展方向。

44226612.article_summary: 苹果公司于2025年6月9日推出全新软件设计，采用名为“Liquid Glass”的新材料，使应用程序和系统体验更具表现力和愉悦感。该设计在iOS 26、iPadOS 26、macOS Tahoe 26、watchOS 26和tvOS 26中实现跨平台统一，同时保持各平台独特性。Liquid Glass材料具有半透明特性，能根据内容和环境动态变化，提升用户对内容的关注度。新的设计包括重新设计的控件、工具栏和导航，适应圆角显示，并通过动态变化使用户更易于操作。系统体验如锁屏、主屏幕等也得到更新，旨在提供更和谐、直观的用户体验。
44226612.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果新推出的半透明“液态玻璃”设计及其影响

不同观点：
• **反对新设计，关注可访问性问题**：
  - [dimal] 认为半透明设计会导致文本难以辨认，特别是对像他这样的自闭症患者不友好，并担心这会广泛影响其他用户。
  - [stalco] 实际安装后，认为设计过于繁杂，设置应用的比例不佳，且对可访问性是“地狱”般的体验。
  - [pardner] 批评新设计过于注重形式而非功能，认为苹果在解决技术债务问题之前不应该推出这种视觉更新。
  - [stevenhubertron] 同样认为新设计在可访问性和可用性上存在严重问题，并表示如果最终设计如此糟糕，可能会放弃使用苹果产品。

• **对新设计持保留态度，但理解其背后的动机**：
  - [designerarvid] 作为用户体验设计师，虽然不完全赞同新设计，但理解其可能是为了吸引年轻一代（尤其是GenZ）用户，并认为这种设计可能是为了传达“高级质量”。
  - [pentagrama] 虽然对新设计的动画效果表示担忧，认为可能导致分心，但也相信苹果会提供关闭选项，且理解这种设计可能是出于营销需求。

• **对新设计持积极态度，认为具有创新潜力**：
  - [captainmuon] 认为新设计利用了现代高分辨率显示器和强大GPU的优势，可以带来更具物理性和现实感的界面设计，只要开发者易于实现这种设计，它有可能成功。
  - [kylehotchkiss] 赞赏苹果在设计上的投入，认为尽管新设计不完美，但可以通过调整对比度来改善，并期待苹果未来在原生UI上的进一步优化。

• **对新设计持怀疑态度，担心历史重演**：
  - [kej] 认为新设计与微软Windows 8的“Metro”设计目标类似，担心苹果会在损害桌面体验的情况下推行这种设计。
  - [ricokatayama] 认为“液态玻璃”设计是苹果设计上的倒退，担心苹果进入“设计地狱”，难以回归简洁有效的设计。

• **历史对比与怀旧情绪**：
  - [StopDisinfo910] 表达了对新设计似曾相识的感觉，联想到早期的Windows Longhorn和Vista设计，认为这是旧设计的新生。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现与未来趋势**：
  - [nharada] 猜测半透明设计可能是为未来的AR界面做准备，因为AR眼镜无法完全显示不透明元素，这种设计可以确保跨平台的一致性。

• **设计历史与影响**：
  - [gherkinnn] 引用了一篇博客，指出新设计与早期Longhorn（后来的Vista）设计相似，表明这种设计趋势早有预测。

争议焦点：
• 新设计的可访问性和可用性问题，特别是对特殊群体（如自闭症患者）的影响。
• 新设计是否过于注重视觉效果而忽视功能性和效率。
• 新设计是否预示着未来AR界面的发展方向。

data.title: Show HN: Most users won't report bugs unless you make it stupidly easy
data.author: lakshikag
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户在软件 bug 报告过程中的体验和问题

不同观点：
• **不愿报告 bug 的原因**：
  - AngryData 和 D13Fd 提到，他们很少报告 bug，除非是新软件或新版本，因为大多数 bug 不会被修复，报告过程感觉像浪费时间。
  - 他们认为，如果公司不重视质量控制（QC），报告 bugs 不会产生实际效果。

• **报告流程的复杂性和垃圾报告问题**：
  - mmsc 指出，过滤无效报告（如无意义或荒谬的报告）是 bug 报告系统的一大挑战，建议采用简单的截图报告和高级报告两种方式。
  - 提出使用 LLM（大型语言模型）过滤无用报告的想法。

• **用户报告 bug 的障碍**：
  - drob518 强调，许多公司没有用户可访问的 bug 报告渠道，用户必须通过客服，这往往是繁琐且无效的。
  - 公司不愿意让用户报告 bug，因为这会暴露开发和测试团队的不足。

• **公司对 bug 报告的回应问题**：
  - supermatt 和 Havoc 提到，公司对 bug 报告的回应往往不足，用户得不到反馈或问题解决，导致用户不愿再次报告。
  - Havoc 还提到，与开发人员进行长时间的调试过程让人疲惫，用户只希望简单指出问题。

• **历史经验和企业态度**：
  - kasajian 分享了曾经向微软报告 bug 的经验，报告 bug 需要通过昂贵的支持服务，虽然最终不会收费，但过程令人却步。
  - 不过，微软后来改进了反馈机制，例如通过 User Voice 和 GitHub Issues。

• **开源项目的 bug 报告**：
  - ryao 提到在开源项目 OpenZFS 中找到并修复了许多 bug，但用户不认为提交 bug 报告值得，这表明用户在不同项目中的报告意愿不同。

• **改进 bug 报告工具的建议**：
  - wittjeff 提出为残障用户设计更容易使用的报告工具，并结合注释功能，提高报告的有效性。
  - rbanffy 分享了在错误页面添加报告按钮以收集更多信息的成功经验。
  - Leo-thorne 提到简化报告表单可以提高报告的数量和质量。

补充讨论：
• **产品设计和用户体验的批评**：
  - infecto 对某些产品页面上的不当文案和 ProductHunt 标志提出批评，认为这影响用户对产品的信任和使用意愿。

争议焦点：用户是否应该花费时间和精力报告 bug，以及公司是否应改进 bug 报告流程和回应机制。用户普遍认为，如果公司不重视 bug 报告，用户就没有义务主动报告问题。

data.title: Hokusai Moyo Gafu: an album of dyeing patterns
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 《北斎模様画譜》是葛饰北斋创作的一本图案集，最初作为染色样品出版，包含许多他设计的原创图案。该书属于日本国立国会图书馆的NDL Image Bank项目，该项目是一个展示日本公共领域艺术品的数字画廊，包含数千件版权过期的作品。NDL Gallery是其在线内容平台，利用国会图书馆的数字化资料提供展览信息，并展示浮世绘、历史照片等各类主题的独特收藏。NDL数字展览则进一步介绍了这些藏品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：葛饰北斋（Hokusai）作品中的艺术风格、图案及其与其他艺术形式（如伊斯兰镶嵌艺术、埃舍尔作品）的潜在联系，以及这些图案的制作方法。

不同观点：
• **[srean]** 提出北斋是否接触过伊斯兰镶嵌艺术的问题，并联想到埃舍尔作品中的对称性和群论。他还提到编织群（braid groups）与北斋作品的潜在联系，并分享了相关博客文章的链接，进一步探讨了与传统舞蹈相关的数学结构。
• **[PaulHouley]** 回应了关于复杂图案的讨论，提到大都会博物馆收藏的 kimono 样本，指出在日本不同历史时期都有复杂且色彩丰富的kimono图案设计，提供了具体的参考链接。
• **[ossicones]** 对北斋作品中“染色图案”的具体应用方法提出疑问，不确定这些图案是通过版画印刷还是通过某种防染技术（如扎染）制作的。
• **[Beijinger]** 直接询问是否有可供下载的PDF版本，关注的是获取这些作品的便捷性问题。
• **[uwagar]** 提出了一个简单的问题，确认这些作品是否出自以《巨浪》闻名的同一葛饰北斋，显示出对作品作者的基本确认需求。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的**链接内容**提供了进一步的背景资料，如编织群在五月柱舞蹈中的应用，为对北斋作品中数学和对称性感兴趣的读者提供了延伸阅读。
• **讨论中的争议焦点**并不明显，但[srean]对北斋与伊斯兰艺术及埃舍尔之间联系的猜测引发了对艺术史跨文化影响的思考。
• **不同评论的讨论关系**：评论间的关系较为松散，[srean]和[PaulHouley]的讨论偏向艺术与数学的联系及历史背景，而[ossicones]和[Beijinger]则更关注具体的技术和获取问题。

总体来看，评论主要围绕北斋作品的艺术风格、图案应用及与其他文化和艺术形式的潜在联系展开。

data.title: A man rebuilding the last Inca rope bridge
data.author: kaonwarb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了秘鲁安第斯山脉中的Q'eswachaka绳索桥，这是世界上仅存的印加手工编织桥之一。每年，当地社区在维克托里亚诺·阿里扎帕纳（Victoriano Arizapana）的带领下，将旧桥拆除并重新编织新桥。这座桥由草和纤维制成，悬挂在60英尺高的河流上方，坚固到可以承载上百人的重量。阿里扎帕纳是这一拥有500多年历史的传统继承人，他是世界上唯一懂得建造此桥的人。文章还提到记者艾略特·斯坦（Eliot Stein）在其书《Custodians of Wonder》中记录了这一古老传统，并探讨了印加帝国的辉煌历史及其复杂的道路系统Qhapaq Ñan。

主要讨论点：关于古老绳索桥的构造及其使用工具的讨论

不同观点：
• **taeric** 认为，在建造桥梁的最后编织过程非常令人惊叹，同时对评论中提到的“轮子没有帮助”的观点表示好奇。他提出，手推车之类的简单带轮工具应该还是有帮助的。此外，他还对不用轮子如何缠绕绳索表示疑问，暗示可能有其他未提及的工具或方法。

• **jmward01** 则从旅游和历史遗迹的角度出发，认为这座桥和马丘比丘一样，是值得参观和体验的有趣地点，侧重于桥梁的文化和观光价值，而非其建造技术细节。

补充讨论：
• **关于轮子的实用性**：taeric 提出了一个技术性的问题，即简单工具如手推车是否可以在桥梁建造过程中发挥作用，质疑原文中“轮子没有帮助”的说法。

• **关于绳索的缠绕方法**：taeric 对没有使用轮子如何缠绕绳索表示不解，暗示在当时的技术条件下可能存在其他有效的工具或技术来进行这种操作。

• **桥梁的文化和历史价值**：jmward01 的评论提醒了讨论中可能忽视的一点，即这座绳索桥不仅是一个工程奇迹，也是具有重要旅游吸引力的历史遗迹，和马丘比丘齐名。

争议焦点：主要集中在建造过程中轮子是否有用以及绳索缠绕方法的合理性上，taeric 对这两个技术细节提出了质疑。

Q'eswachaka Rope Bridge
Keshwa chaca, among the last handwoven Incan bridges, crosses Apurimac Canyon in Peru.

Every year, high in the
Andes Mountains in Peru, a man builds a bridge. The bridge is strong enough to hold the weight of more than one hundred men. But it isn’t made of iron or steel. It’s made of grasses and fibers. It hangs 60 feet above a thundering river.
And the man is not a construction worker or a structural engineer—but he is the only person on earth who knows how to build this particular bridge. That man’s name is Victoriano Arizapana, and he is the heir to a tradition that is over 500 years old.
The Inca Empire built elaborate rope bridges to cross vast chasms in the Andes.
Today, only one of those bridges remains: the Q’eswachaka. Every single year since the Inca Empire, Victoriano’s family has led the local community in cutting the bridge down and reweaving it from scratch.
I’m Dylan Thuras, and this is Atlas Obscura.
This is an edited transcript of the
Atlas Obscura Podcast
: a celebration of the world’s strange, incredible, and wondrous places. Find the show on
Apple Podcasts
,
Spotify
, and all major podcast apps.
The view from the Q’eswachaka woven suspension bridge.
Dylan Thuras / Atlas Obscura
Dylan Thuras:
We often hear about the first person to do something—an inventor, a pioneer. It’s rarer to hear about the last person to carry on a tradition. Today, I’m talking with Eliot Stein. He’s a journalist for the BBC, and he traveled across the world reporting on rare and ancient practices and talking to the final stewards keeping these traditions alive.
It includes a visit to one of the greatest places that I have ever been in my life—a place sometimes called the Last Incan Bridge, but better known as the Q’eswachaka. Eliot chronicled this in his book,
Custodians of Wonder: Ancient Customs, Profound Traditions, and the Last People Keeping Them Alive
.
Hey, Eliot. Thanks for joining.
Eliot Stein:
Hey, thanks so much for having me.
Dylan:
Yeah. Your book is called
Custodians of Wonder
. What drew you to this subject matter?
Eliot:
I had this chance encounter 20 years ago that effectively changed my life. I was leading tours in Italy, and off an island near Venice called Burano, I came across this 90-year-old woman who, for whatever reason, took an interest in me and led me into her home.
She was blind, and she asked me to take a look at her life’s work, which was hung up on the wall. It was lace, but it was very clear to me that I’d never seen anything like this. It looked sort of like stitched seafoam or embroidered spider webs. I was asking her to tell me about this, and it quickly became clear to me that it wasn’t just beautiful, but for 300 years, this lace that was only made on this one small island was one of the most coveted items in the Western world.
It was the boast of royalty, the height of fashion, the target of international smuggling—but more than anything, for this rather anonymous group of women, it was their life. It was their pride. It was something that means something to them.
This kind of awakened in me this sympathy, this reverence for these final custodians who—the woman’s name was Anna—all she wanted was for visitors like myself to understand what makes this island so special; and that was really what drew me to this as a way to kind of quietly cast a light on people who are humble, are anonymous, but have given something beautiful to the world.
Dylan:
It’s a great book, and I think we’re going to be covering a number of stories from this book on the show over time. But today, we’re going to talk about one of my favorite places that I’ve ever been, one of the coolest people I’ve ever met. We’re going to be talking about Victoriano Arizapana, the bridgekeeper, and the Q’eswachaka, sometimes called the Last Incan Bridge.
But to understand the story, I think you really have to start with the Incan Empire. It’s one of the world’s most fascinating civilizations. It develops in basically relative isolation and becomes one of the largest empires in the world at the time.
So maybe we could start by talking about how that happened.
Eliot:
The way that they did that was through this incredible road system called the Qhapaq Ñan, which means the Royal Road in Quechua. And the Royal Road was rivaled only in history by the Roman road system.
And at its height, it spanned 40,000 kilometers, which is roughly the circumference of the globe. It was an incredible feat of engineering, and compared to the Roman road system—which traversed a relatively uniform topography—the Inca Empire went from the snow-capped peaks of the Andes down to the steamy basin of the Amazon.
And to do that, these people who didn’t have wheels, mortar, written language, they bore massive tunnels through the mountains. They paved stones so that they were as clear

data.title: Urban living expands musical tastes but reduces shared preferences, study finds
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 一项由康奈尔大学、Deezer Research和德国马普研究所组成的国际团队研究发现，城市生活扩展了人们的音乐品味，但同时也减少了共享的音乐偏好。研究分析了来自法国、巴西和德国250万用户的2.5亿条听歌记录，结果显示，都市居民的音乐品味更加多样化，且与邻居的共同偏好减少。研究还发现，人们的“听歌半径”（即听歌类型和艺术家的广泛程度）在二十多岁时达到巅峰，之后逐渐缩小。大城市的多元人口和文化交流促进了音乐多样性，即使控制了人口统计差异，大城市依然表现出更大的音乐差异性。这表明，城市环境和体验本身对音乐多样性有重要影响。研究发表于《Nature Communications》。

If your commute involves packed subway cars, chances are your headphones are piping something rather different from your seatmate's. A new study analyzing individuals' listening patterns suggests that urban living not only exposes people to a wider array of sounds, but also pulls listeners apart, taste-wise, from those sitting right beside them.
An international team, including scientists from Cornell University, Deezer Research in Paris and Max Planck Institutes in Germany, sifted through 250 million listening logs from 2.5 million users in France, Brazil and Germany and determined that living in a metropolis broadens our musical horizons, and makes our playlists less alike. Their study, "Mechanisms of Cultural Diversity in Urban Populations," was
published
in
Nature Communications
.
The work was done in collaboration with Deezer Research in Paris. Deezer is a global music streaming platform available in 187 countries featuring over 90 million tracks.
"This paper is particularly special as it represents a rare
collaboration
between academia and industry, giving us access to individual-level interaction data from millions of users. We used this unique dataset to investigate what makes cities culturally diverse," said co-author Nori Jacoby, assistant professor of psychology in the College of Arts & Sciences and group leader at the Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics.
Demographic variables largely account for the diversity in the most populous areas and reveal distinctions between BID and WID. Credit:
Nature Communications
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-60538-2
The research team measured diversity of music across
urban populations
in two ways. First, they looked at how similar (or not) the songs played by people in the same area were. Across all three countries, the larger the city, the more distinct people's musical tastes were from their neighbors. They found there's less of a single, shared musical taste in big cities.
"A resident of Paris, for instance, shared far fewer tracks with other Parisians than listeners in Orne (a region in northwest France) did with their neighbors," said Harin Lee, corresponding author and Jacoby's doctoral student.
The researchers also calculated each individual's "listening radius"—roughly how far they roamed across genres and artists. They found that people living in larger urban areas also tend to listen to a broader variety of music, expanding their personal musical repertoire.
The study also found that this listening radius changes over the course of life. When the researchers lined up listeners by age, they saw a near-perfect bell curve. Musical radius expands rapidly from the mid-teens, reaches its widest span in the late-twenties, and then contracts, slowly but surely, through midlife and beyond. The team found the exact same inverted-U pattern in France, Germany and Brazil, even after stripping out auto-play tracks and other algorithmic nudges.
Individuals’ music listening is more distinct from one another in large metropolitan areas, resulting in dispersed pockets of diverse music interests. Credit:
Nature Communications
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-60538-2
According to Lee, the twenties are when people typically leave home and meet new people, as well as having time and an interest in exploring. After 30, responsibilities mount, spare hours shrink, and the playlists built during our exploratory years can solidify into habit.
But the study shows that fifty-year-olds still roam far wider than most teenagers. They may have simply begun to circle the artists and eras that resonate most.
To explain the difference in big-city listening habits, the researchers assembled a detailed demographic portrait of each city, covering everything from age, income and immigrant share to average Facebook-friend counts and the number of nearby music venues.
Through computational models accounting for all these factors, the team concluded that the demographic mixing in cities contributes to the musical diversity, especially in the very largest cities, but that wasn't the full story. The researchers speculate that the differences in listening habits could be partly because of a lack of cultural resources in more rural areas.
"Even after controlling for these demographic differences, larger cities still fostered greater musical variety," Jacoby said. "This suggests there is something about the urban interactions and experience itself is at play."

data.title: The new Gödel Prize winner tastes great and is less filling
data.author: baruchel
data.article_summary: Eshan Chattopadhyay和David Zuckerman因其论文《Explicit two-source extractors and resilient functions》荣获2025年Gödel奖。该论文发表于STOC 2016，并于2019年刊登在《Annals of Math》。Bill和Lance对该成果感兴趣出于不同原因。Bill关注其在构造性拉姆齐理论中的应用，而Lance则强调其在伪随机性方面的贡献，特别是从两个低最小熵独立源中提取接近完美随机比特的能力。该成果改进了构造性拉姆齐数的界限，提出了指数级别的改进，达到了$2^{(\log k)^\epsilon}$。尽管Bill认为该成果在伪随机化和拉姆齐理论中都有重要应用，Lance则更看重其在伪随机性方面的主要 beauty。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对博客帖子内容、获奖论文的技术背景以及相关理论的讨论

不同观点：
• NooneAtAll3认为帖子内容不明确，没有清楚地解释获奖论文的具体内容，以及“extractor”和“resilient function”等术语的定义。他还质疑帖子为何转向讨论Ramsey理论，并觉得一半的篇幅在重复之前博客中讨论过的话题，显得浪费。

• HPMOR对这个获奖消息感到兴奋，尤其是看到自己的算法教授获奖，表达了对获奖者的祝贺。

• bhasi补充了背景信息，提到获奖者Eshan的学士论文导师Prof Manindra Agrawal也曾于2006年获得Gödel奖，强调了学术上的传承和成就。

• Horde表示这个帖子让他想起了STOC（Symposium on Theory of Computing），并计划阅读过去几年的会议论文。他还提到2026年STOC将在美国举行，并对一些技术性强的论文表示兴趣。

• antics提供了一个技术性的解释，回答了如何用有偏差的硬币模拟真正的随机硬币抛掷，并借此介绍了“randomness extractors”的概念，进一步解释了新获得Gödel奖的论文在该领域的贡献。

• doctorpangloss从一个更广泛的角度讨论了学习高难度数学课程（如Math 55）带来的现实世界机会，特别是与支付领域相关的风险投资机会，暗示了数学教育的实际应用价值。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对技术术语和概念的解释需求，特别是“randomness extractors”和Gödel奖获奖论文的具体贡献。
• 对学术成就的祝贺和相关背景信息的补充，显示出对学术界杰出人物和事件的关注。
• 讨论中还涉及到对未来学术会议的期待和过往会议论文的阅读兴趣。
• 最后，有人将高水平数学教育与现实世界机会联系起来，扩展了讨论的范围。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于博客帖子的内容是否清晰和有价值，特别是NooneAtAll3对帖子内容重复和术语解释不清表示不满。

44224996.article_content:
David Zuckerman
The 2025 Gödel Prize
has been awarded
to Eshan Chattopadhyay and David Zuckerman for their paper
Explicit two-source extractors and resilient functions
which was in
STOC 2016
and in the
Annals of Math
in 2019.
We (Bill and Lance) care about this result for two different reasons.
BILL: The result has applications to constructive Ramsey---
LANCE: Ramsey Theory? Really? This is a great result about
Eshan Chattopadhyay
pseudorandomness! In fact the only interesting thing to come out of Ramsey Theory is the Probabilistic Method (see our discussion of this
here
).
BILL: Can't it be BOTH a great result in derandomization AND have an application to Ramsey Theory. Like Miller Lite: Less Filling AND Tastes Great (see
here
)
LANCE: But you don't drink!
BILL: Which means I can give a sober description of their application to Ramsey Theory.
All statements are asymptotic.
Let \(R(k)\) be the least \(n\) so that for all 2-colorings of \(K_n\) there is a homog set of size \(k\).
Known and easy: \(R(k)\le 2^{2k}/\sqrt{k} \)
Known and hard: \(R(k) \le 3.993^k \). How do I know this is true? Either I believe the survey papers on these kinds of results (see
here
) or a former student of mine emailed me a picture of a T-shirt that has the result (see
here
) from (of course) Hungary.
Known and Easy and Non-Constructive: \(R(k)\ge k2^{k/2}\)
Can we get a constructive proof? There were some over the years; however, the paper by Eshan Chattopadhyay and David Zuckerman improves the constructive bound to exponential in \(  2^{(\log k)^\epsilon}.\)
SO Lance, why do you care?
LANCE: First of all when I chose this paper as one of my
favorite theorems
(a far bigger honor than the so-called Gödel Prize) I gave the post the clever title
Extracting Ramsey Graphs
that captures both the pseudorandomness and the Ramsey graphs. But of course the Ramsey result is just a minor corollary, the ability to get a near perfect random bit out of two independent sources of low min-entropy is the true beauty of this paper.
BILL: You have no sense of good taste.
LANCE: Well at least I'm not less filling.

data.title: Meta to pay $15B to acquire 49% stake in Scale AI/hire Scale CEO
data.author: htrp
data.article_summary: Meta正计划对人工智能公司Scale AI进行近150亿美元的投资，以获取其49%的股份，并招募Scale AI的CEO Alexandr Wang加入Meta团队。此举旨在加速Meta在人工智能领域的发展，特别是实现人工通用智能（AGI）。AGI是指达到或超越人类认知能力的人工智能，是当前各大科技公司竞相追求的目标。由于竞争对手如OpenAI、Anthropic、Google和Microsoft在AI技术上的领先，Meta担心自身落后，因此通过投资Scale AI来增强竞争力。Scale AI主要为行业巨头提供训练数据，预计2025年收入将翻倍至约20亿美元，并正计划以250亿美元的估值进行融资。此外，Scale AI还与多国政府达成合作，包括为卡塔尔提供自动化工具以及与美国国防部签订AI项目合同。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta（Facebook母公司）接近以近150亿美元投资Scale AI，获得49%的股份，此举旨在加速其人工智能（AI）特别是通用人工智能（AGI）的发展目标。

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：该投资主要是为了获取Scale AI的数据和数据标注团队。这种观点认为，Meta的投资并不是单纯为了技术合作，而是看重Scale AI所拥有的海量数据及其处理能力，这对于训练AI模型至关重要。评论中提到"49% stake to effectively buy Scale's data + the data labeling team"（49%的股份实际上是为了购买Scale的数据和数据标注团队），表明有人认为数据是这次投资的核心。
  
• 第二种观点：投资的重点在于获取顶尖AI人才和加速AGI的研发。根据Bloomberg和The New York Times的报道，Mark Zuckerberg亲自组建了一个约50人的团队来推动Meta的AI目标，特别是实现通用人工智能（AGI）。这一观点认为，Meta的投资更侧重于人才和技术上的合作，以增强其在AI领域的竞争力。

• 其他观点：有人可能认为这次投资是Meta为了在AI领域追赶竞争对手（如Google、OpenAI）的战略性举动。通过投资Scale AI，Meta能够快速获得外部创新资源，弥补自身在AI技术上的不足。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点：投资的真正目的到底是获取数据还是技术和人才。部分评论可能认为，Meta主要看重的是Scale AI的数据资源，而其他人则强调技术和人才的重要性。
  
• 投资规模和结构：近150亿美元的投资和49%的股份表明Meta对Scale AI的高度重视，但也有人可能会质疑这一大规模投资的风险，尤其是在AI技术发展尚不确定的情况下。
  
• 法律和监管问题：如此大规模的投资和跨公司合作可能会引起反垄断和数据隐私方面的监管审查，特别是在当前对科技巨头监管日益严格的环境下。

总结：Meta对Scale AI的投资引发了关于其真实目的的讨论，有人认为是为了数据，有人认为是为了技术和人才，同时法律和监管问题也是值得关注的讨论点。

News
Meta is reportedly making a $15 billion bet on AGI
Zuckerberg is said to be buying nearly half of Scale AI — and recruiting the company’s CEO, too
Zuckerberg is said to be buying nearly half of Scale AI — and recruiting the company’s CEO, too
by
Hayden Field
Jun 10, 2025, 4:22 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Hayden Field
is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets.
Meta is close to finalizing an almost $15 billion investment in Scale AI, the tech giant’s largest-ever external investment, which would give Meta a 49% stake in the company,
according to
The Information
. As part of the deal, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is personally assembling a team of about 50 people to help Meta supercharge its AI goals — specifically, to achieve artificial general intelligence — and Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang is set to join that group once the deal is final, according to
Bloomberg
and
The New York Times
.
AGI is the concept of AI that equals or surpasses human cognitive abilities, and it’s something that nearly every AI industry leader is currently racing to achieve before their competitors.
Bloomberg
was first to report on the planned multibillion-dollar investment.
Scale, the AI giant that provides training data to industry leaders like OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Meta, in April
reportedly
expected that its 2025 revenue would more than double year-over-year to about $2 billion. It’s also currently planning a tender offer for employees and early investors at a $25 billion valuation.
Meta has been concerned about falling behind in the AI race as competitors like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft pull ahead. In May, Meta
delayed
the launch of its new flagship model, dubbed Behemoth, amid concerns about its capabilities compared to competing models,
The Wall Street Journal
reported.
The company’s investment in Scale AI is likely a bid to catch up as competing tech giants each choose one or more AI startups to back for greater chances of AI success, whether internally or externally.
Amazon has invested at least $8 billion in Anthropic, the AI startup founded by ex-OpenAI research executives, and Anthropic’s tech now powers Amazon’s Alexa Plus. Google has given at least $3 billion to Anthropic, and the two companies share a significant cloud contract. Microsoft has famously invested at least $13 billion in OpenAI and currently gets a share of the company’s revenue.
Besides its forthcoming deal with Meta, Scale has spent the last few months leaning hard into deals with governments across the world, like a five-year deal with Qatar to provide automation tools for civil service, healthcare, and more. The company has said its work with countries in Asia and Europe could account for a big piece of sales coming up. And in March, Scale signed a multimillion-dollar deal with the Department of Defense for a flagship AI agent program for the U.S. military.
